provenance.source: Taxes Consolidation Act 1997; Finance Act 2026; KPMG and Revenue summaries of Budget 2026; PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Ireland
provenance.notes: The EUR 44,000 standard rate band came from PwC. The credits, USC bands and the PRSI increase from 1 October 2026 came from Budget 2026 summaries, read on 31 August 2026.

omissions: Single individuals only. The increased standard rate band for married couples and single parents is not modelled.
The reduced USC rate for medical card holders and people over 70 is not modelled.
Rent tax credit, mortgage interest relief and the home carer credit are not modelled.
The PRSI weekly credit that tapers the charge for low earners is not modelled.

incomeTax.note: Only two rates, but they bite early: the 40% rate starts at EUR 44,000 for a single person.

credits.note: Ireland grants credits against the tax rather than allowances against income, so they are worth the same to every taxpayer regardless of rate.

usc.note: A separate charge with its own bands, levied on gross income before pension relief. Below the exemption threshold no USC is due at all - and then it is due on the whole income, not just the excess.

prsi.legalRef: Social Welfare Consolidation Act 2005, Class A
prsi.note: The employee rate rises on 1 October 2026, so the same monthly pay costs more in the last quarter of the year than in the first three.

regions.name: Ireland
regions.note: Irish income tax has no regional component.

inputSchema.label: Gross pay (per month)
inputSchema.help: Gross monthly pay. The month matters here: the employee PRSI rate rises from 4.2% to 4.35% on 1 October 2026.

inputSchema.label: PAYE income tax deducted (per month)
inputSchema.help: Income tax only, not USC or PRSI. Used for the annual comparison.

inputSchema.label: Pension contributions
inputSchema.help: Contributions within your age-related limit get relief against income tax, but NOT against USC or PRSI, which are charged on your pay before pension relief.
